requirement:
The view of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes` MUST show
each `habeas:coverage` citation attached to the file root or an explicitly
declared function or method. Each entry MUST identify its source item and
source location and show the fenced citation commentary and Rust doc comments
supplying its tracked justification under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.anchor`.
When no tracked justification is present, the entry MUST say so.

File-root citations MUST be labelled as file-threshold exception proposals;
function and method citations MUST be labelled as function exception proposals,
following {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.anchor`.
rationale: The reviewed tests adequately cover `requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes.justifications`. **Obligations and the tests that cover them** - **Show each citation on a file root or declared function or method.** - `notes_show_root_function_and_method_proposals_with_owned_commentary_and_docs` has a file-root citation, a free function and an impl method. It checks all three headings: `File root`, `fn[ordinary]` and `impl[Worker]/fn[work]`. - The same test has a citation on a nested module. It asserts that the module's commentary ("Nested module must…") and the child's docs ("Child documentation") do not appear. - `citations_on_modules_and_citation_text_in_literals_do_not_create_explanations` checks that a citation on a module, or citation text inside a string literal, creates no entry. - `documentation_includes_non_rust_functions_methods_and_plain_file_roots` covers Python, TypeScript and plain-file items. - **Identify the source item and source location.** - The notes test checks each entry's `Source: code.rs:{first}–{last}` range. - It also checks each entry's "First source citation at line N". The four entries are checked individually. - **Show fenced commentary and Rust doc comments that supply the justification.** - The notes test checks root `//!` docs, function `///` docs and method `/** */` docs. - It also checks fenced commentary for the root, function and method, including HTML escaping of ``. - `justification_can_come_from_docs_or_fenced_commentary_but_not_ordinary_comments` has three cases: docs alone, fenced commentary alone, and ordinary comments alone. Each case checks the matching `### Rust doc comments` or `### Citation commentary` heading, or the absence of both. - **Say so when no tracked justification is present.** - In the notes test, the bare `{cite}` on `fn[unexplained]` is the only entry with "No tracked justification is present." The test counts that message exactly once and checks it inside that entry. It also checks that the entry has no "Rust doc comments" section. - The ordinary-comment case in the justification test also asserts the message. - **Label file roots as file-threshold proposals and functions and methods as function proposals.** The notes test asserts exactly one "File-threshold exception proposal" and exactly three "Function exception proposal" labels. That matches one root, plus the function, method and unexplained function. **Residual considerations** - I did not find a test for a file root with no justification. In `fn[entry]` in `src/execution_coverage/notes.rs`, the "no justification" branch does not depend on whether the item is a root. It depends only on empty commentary and empty docs, so the function-level test exercises the same code. I do not treat this as a gap. - The non-Rust test checks that the output contains the item names and explanations. It does not check labels. This is acceptable because the Rust-based tests assert the labels and the entry code is shared. I found no unacknowledged gap.

:::{req} check.exceptions.anchor
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:coverage` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:
> Cite this on a source file or explicitly declared function to propose a
> coverage exception. Explain in prose why the item's incomplete execution
> coverage is acceptable. Put the explanation in fenced citation commentary
> or Rust doc comments included in the source item's assessed input. An ordinary
> non-doc comment alone does not supply a tracked justification. The reason
> must be substantive; difficulty alone is not a justification.
> On a file's root item, the exception excuses only
> that file's 80% instrumented-line threshold, including absent measurement
> of its executable code. On an explicit function with a body, it excuses
> that function's recorded zero execution or absence from otherwise usable
> measurement, without excusing the file's threshold.
> The explanation must agree with the current source and any callers or
> configuration assumptions on which it relies. Only a current accepted
> independent assessment permits the exception. A file exception does not
> excuse unexecuted or not-measured functions in that file.
> The citation applies to its source item without conditional build matching
> and may remain when measured coverage satisfies the item's obligations.
Only `{cite}` MAY reference this built-in, inline or fenced using the standard
reference forms of {cite}`requirements.references.roles`. The built-in MUST be
available in every project without a project requirement, site query, or
exception-specific configuration.
